text: Never let any Government imagine that it can choose perfectly safe courses; rather let it expect to have to take very doubtful ones, because it is found in ordinary affairs that one never seeks to avoid one trouble without running into another; but prudence consists in knowing how to distinguish the character of troubles, and for choice to take the lesser evil.
author: Niccolo Machiavelli
locator: Chapter XXI, How a prince should conduct himself so as to gain renown
location: Sant'Andrea in Percussina, near Florence, Italy
